question: Should OpenClaw adopt this private final-capture recovery contract in core now, including the selected-agent inventory and host-supplied closure-evidence boundary, or wait for the RFC and aggregate recovery-point owners to settle those interfaces?
rationale: The patch intentionally defines a new lifecycle/state ownership boundary rather than repairing an established behavior, and the linked dependency and RFC are still open.

options.title: Pause for RFC ownership approval
options.body: Keep this stacked PR open but do not merge until the RFC and aggregate recovery-point ownership and acceptance contracts are explicitly approved.

options.title: Accept the narrow core contract
options.body: Approve the private command and its state boundary as the core-owned portion of the handoff design, then require a rebase and runtime proof before merge.

recommendation.title: Pause for RFC ownership approval
recommendation.body: Keep this stacked PR open but do not merge until the RFC and aggregate recovery-point ownership and acceptance contracts are explicitly approved.

likelyOwner.reason: They can clarify the intended split across the linked stacked recovery-point proposals, while repository owners make the final product decision.
